from the 0.199.0 window as written by hand, the harness line mid-Changed. -->
# Changelog

Head prose.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Fleet access: each machine decides what the other machines of its fleet may do to it, and
  starts at Read Only.** A machine's fleet access is one of three levels. Read Only: the others
  read it (`survey`, `await task`, a session's status, text, screen, result and inbox), and none
  starts a job, sends a message or types into a session there. Read and Write, No New Tabs: they
  also message, type into, take over and close the sessions already there. Full Access: they
  also start new jobs and tabs. `aterm fleet access` prints the level and `aterm fleet access
  read|write|full` sets it, on that machine only; a worker another machine started there can
  lower it and never raise it. A level is chosen for one fleet: `aterm fleet leave`, and an
  `init`, a `join` or a `sync` that writes another fleet's key (an `init --rotate` included),
  put it back to Read Only and say so, while the same fleet joined or synced again and its
  rotated secret keep it. It caps the
  drive grants without changing them, so raising a machine to Full Access brings back what its
  grants allowed before. Every `survey` header says the level (`access=read|write|full`), and
  `aterm ctl --host any spawn` picks only machines at Full Access. `aterm help fleet` (FLEET
  ACCESS) has the whole table, the four fleet services the level does not govern (vault
  approval, service repair, account renewal, the sign-in challenge relay), and what it does not
  cover: ssh, Screen Sharing and any process running as the account.

- **Windows: `aterm update` installs a build staged on this PC.** Windows downloads nothing and
  still has no network updater or public build: a build loop on the PC (`aterm-winship update`,
  below) stages one under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\aterm\dist`. `aterm update status` and `aterm update
  check` name the build you run and the staged one: its version, commit, build number, when it was
  staged and its smoke-test verdict. `aterm update apply` installs it and stops nothing: open
  windows keep running the build they started with, and new windows and shells use the new one.
  `aterm update apply --restart` saves the open windows, installs and starts aterm again. While a
  staged build is not what is installed, did not fail its smoke test and can be installed over
  this copy, the tab strip's version label is marked and the Version menu and the command palette
  offer "Install ... now". Once it is installed under an open window (by the loop, by `apply` in a
  shell or by another window), the offer comes down and the window says the build is installed and
  to restart aterm to move onto it; `apply` then answers that it is already installed. An offer
  whose build failed or went missing comes down without a message. A copy `apply` cannot install
  over (one in an MSIX package, one run from a dist folder or a cargo build folder, or a dist with
  no `install.ps1`) is told why, and `aterm ctl update status` says the same (`staged=`,
  `installed_build=`, `outcome=`).

### Changed

- **`targo --unverified verify land` stops a judgment main has already outdated.** While the
  dev set runs, the land reads origin's main at each stage the run reports and at least every
  3 minutes. The first main tip whose new commits touch the branch's files ends the run there
  (an `INTERRUPTED` line, and an `Aterm-Interrupted` trailer rather than an `Aterm-Checked`
  one), and the land merges that tip and judges it at once, as one of its three re-judges.
  Before, the run went on to its end, often an hour or more, only to be judged again. A tip
  that still composes, and a run that has already reported a red, are left to finish.

- **A crate whose edits are only comments is judged alone.** `targo --unverified verify`
  counted a changed comment as changed code, so a comment edit in a widely used crate ran
  every crate that depends on it. A crate whose files now differ only in plain or doc comments,
  every other token on its line and column, runs its own full rows (lint too, which reads
  `SAFETY` comments) and its dependents run nothing; the cone names it `<crate> (alone)`. A
  member `Cargo.toml` edited without changing its parsed value counts the same way. A comment a
  macro may read (in a macro's arguments or body, on an item with a derive, an attribute macro
  or a `#[doc = …]`, in a Trust `clean` island or an `include!` target) still selects the
  dependents, as does any edit that moves code.

- **Harness versions since v0.198.0: `alab claude harness 0.34`, `alab agy harness 0.18`, `alab grok harness 0.20`, `alab muse harness 0.21`.** Each harness's minor moves once per release in which it changed.

- **The footer's folder, branch and context no longer take a click, and everything that does
  looks one way under the pointer.** A click on `⌂` the folder, `⎇` the branch or `◐` the
  context used to hide it; it now does nothing, the pointer stays an arrow there and the fact
  looks as it does at rest, so a stray click can no longer take a fact off the line. A
  right-click still opens each one's card (copy, a new tab there, compact), and so do Return
  and Space on one the keyboard selected. Every part of the footer a click acts on (the chips,
  the model, the effort, the account and usage, the quota row, the harness switch, the
  top-effort key) now shows it the same way under the pointer or the keyboard's selection: its
  words in the lit ink over one underline that runs from its first glyph to its last, with no
  change of weight; a warning keeps its warning ink and a chart is left as it was. The hand
  shows over exactly the underlined cells: the blanks around the harness switch's `● on`, and
  before and after the quota row's words, are no longer part of the click.

### Removed

- **Click-to-hide on the footer's folder, branch and context, and the Hide rows on their
  cards.** Nothing on those three hides them any more. Where a program starts with one of them
  off the line (Muse and Kimi show their own), its dimmed mark still brings it back with a
  click, and there its card keeps the one row that puts it away again. The `▸` the top-effort
  key wore while the keyboard had it is gone too: the key now takes the same look as every
  other selected part.

### Fixed

- **`agh repo fetch-ref --checkout-closure` works with Ubuntu 24.04's git.** Its filtered
  fetch makes agh's scratch repository a promisor of the source, and with lazy fetching off
  git 2.43.0 stops a presence read at the first blob the checkout cache lacks ("could not
  fetch … from promisor remote") where git 2.56.0 answers `missing`, so every closure
  over a cache missing a blob failed with "could not inspect the complete checkout cache
  batch". agh reads blob presence through an empty repository whose object store is the
  scratch's and which names no promisor, so a git answers `missing` and cannot fetch.

- **A newly installed build whose recovery proof keeps being refused no longer holds every
  update forever.** After a swap the new build proves its rollback copy before it settles its
  boot trial; when that proof was refused every time (a rollback bundle it could not verify or
  remove), the trial stayed armed and each later update waited behind it with no end. The
  running build now counts the refusals: after 3 of them across 30 awake minutes it settles the
  trial without the proof, keeps the build (it is never reverted for this) and lets updates
  continue; `aterm update status` says so while it waits. A confirmation the updater cannot
  answer (its worker is busy or gone, an answer never arrives) is retried 5 times and then
  leaves the decision to the apply itself, which names what holds it. The previous build then
  stays on disk until the next update replaces it. Some holds are left without a bound on
  purpose: a window that never draws its first frame, a trial file the filesystem will not
  remove, and an installed bundle that no longer verifies as the running build while the
  previous one does, which the third launch still reverts.
